title: Ambient artificial intelligence scribes in dentistry
html: Digital transformation in dentistry continues to accelerate, yet a gap remains between the promise of electronic dental records (EDRs) and their real-world performance. Despite widespread adoption, the quality, completeness, and interoperability of dental data still lag behind medical systems, limiting continuity of care and secondary uses such as surveillance and clinical decision support.1,2 In their commentary, Pethani and colleagues2 highlighted ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes as an emerging response to this challenge, with the potential to improve documentation quality while reducing clinician cognitive burden.
